name: Civil Interfaces for Equipment & Services

activities: survey grid lines & benchmarks
coordinate equipment / anchor positions from vendor GA & loading drawings
sequence.note: Positions come from approved vendor loading/anchor drawings.

activities: excavate
blinding & sub-base for foundations, trenches, pits
set anchor bolts / templates, embedded plates, cast-in conduits, sleeves, earthing tape, HD-bolt boxes to survey before pour
sequence.note: Cast-in items go in before concrete — they cannot be added afterwards.

activities: reinforcement
formwork
cast-in items check
foundations, plinths, housekeeping pads, pedestals, pits, trenches, equipment-room slabs
cure to design strength
strip formwork
grout-pocket / shim prep
as-built survey of anchor bolts, levels & pockets vs vendor tolerance
release for equipment setting / steel erection
form / core wall & slab penetrations
sleeves for pipe, cable & duct crossings
cable trenches, duct banks, manholes, pull-pits for underground services
equipment / electrical-room shell, floor levels, bunds, sumps, blockouts ready for MEP fit-out
backfill, trench covers
non-shrink grout under base plates after equipment is set & aligned
sequence.note: Grouting follows equipment setting, not before.

typical_relationships.reason: Cast-in items cannot be fixed without approved positions and loads.

typical_relationships.before: embeds / anchor bolts / sleeves set & surveyed
typical_relationships.reason: Cast-in items must be in place before concrete — they cannot be added later.

typical_relationships.before: foundation poured & cured to design strength
typical_relationships.reason: Equipment is set on a foundation that has reached strength.
Misplaced anchor bolts stop the equipment set and force rework.

typical_relationships.after: pipe / cable / duct routing through them
typical_relationships.reason: Penetrations must exist before services can cross the structure.

typical_relationships.before: cable trenches / duct banks & manholes complete
typical_relationships.reason: Cables pull through a completed trench / duct route.

typical_relationships.after: MEP equipment installation in the room
typical_relationships.reason: The room must be weathertight and level before fit-out.
Grout is placed after the equipment is set and aligned, not before.

interfaces.requirement: Foundation cured to strength and anchor bolts surveyed before equipment setting / alignment.
Foundation strength & grouting complete before imposing dynamic / rotating loads.
Anchor bolts & base-plate levels set and surveyed before steel erection.
Cable trenches, duct banks, sleeves & openings ready before cable pulling / tray routing.
Duct banks & pull-pits complete before power/MV cable pulling.
Pipe-rack footings, sleeper foundations & sleeves ready before rack piping.
Builders-work openings, sleeves & plant-room slabs ready before MEP rough-in.
Earth pits and cast-in earth tape / electrodes placed before pour & backfill.

testing_requirements: Concrete compressive strength (cube / cylinder) to design before loading
As-built survey of anchor bolts, embed plates & levels vs vendor tolerance
Non-shrink grout compressive strength under base plates
Duct-bank / pull-pit mandrel & rodding test before cable pulling
Trench / pit water-tightness and bund integrity where required
commissioning_dependencies: Not commissioned, but the gating enabler — no equipment set, no cable pulled, no MEP rough-in until foundation strength, anchor survey, openings and trenches are signed off
Grout cured before running rotating / dynamic equipment
Earthing embeds & pits placed before backfill (cannot be added retrospectively)
typical_exceptions: Skid / packaged units may sit on a simple pad with minimal foundation, compressing civil scope
Pure building / architectural civil (finishes, superstructure) is out of scope — only equipment- and service-enabling civil

work_packages.note: Positions driven by mechanical/electrical vendor data.

evidence: Equipment setting, cable pulling or MEP rough-in is scheduled before its civil interface — foundation strength, surveyed anchor bolts, or wall/slab openings — is complete, forcing rework or blocking the trade.
